Use an automatic Monkhorst-Pack k-point grid with a half shift in all directions.

Choose the k-point grid density yourself, selecting a sampling dense enough for a converged variable-cell relaxation of a 10-atom perovskite cell.
Handle magnetism appropriately: BiFeO3 with these inputs provides no starting magnetization, so run the relaxation as a standard (non-magnetic or default-start) calculation consistent with the provided settings, without adding Hubbard U or spin-orbit coupling since none are specified.
After the vc-relax converges, run an SCF calculation on the fully relaxed structure using the same pseudopotentials, cutoffs, convergence thresholds, and k-point grid.
